title: ccpool pools
description: ccpool sessions grouped by pool (the basename of the pool directory). The pool variable lists the pools that report capacity, and All expands to those pools. A series with no pgrouter_role label is shown as unlabelled.

panels.title: Live sessions
panels.description: Live ccpool sessions across the selected pools and roles. A bad value is a count that is 0 while work is queued, or one that sits at the pool maximum.

panels.title: Awaiting human
panels.description: Live sessions waiting for input. Any value above 0 means a person is needed. Zero is shown only while the exporter is reporting capacity; a dead exporter shows No data, not a green 0.

targets.expr: sum(max by (state, live, pool, pgrouter_role) (last_over_time(ccpool_session_states{state="needs_input",live="true"}[35m]))) or (vector(0) and on() (max(last_over_time(ccpool_pool_capacity[35m])) >= 0))

panels.title: Pool free capacity
panels.description: Free launch slots across the selected pools (ccpool_pool_capacity dim free; the ceiling is dim max_sessions, shown in Capacity live vs max). 0 means no new session can start.

panels.title: Worktrees
panels.description: Handler worktrees on disk (the janitor census). A count that keeps climbing means worktrees are leaking.

panels.title: Worktree size (GB)
panels.description: Total size of the handler worktrees in GB (a lower bound when the scan is cut short). A fast-growing value means a leak or an oversized checkout.

panels.title: Worktree scan
panels.description: Whether the last worktree census finished. A lower bound means it hit its time or entry budget, so the count and size are minimums.

panels.title: Versions
panels.description: The running version of each ccpool component, from ccpool_build_info. An unexpected or dev/unknown version means a deploy did not take.

panels.title: Janitor last success age
panels.description: Time since the janitor last finished a pass successfully. Amber above 20 minutes, red above 30 minutes means the janitor is stale or failing. window: fixed - the 7d lookback only has to outlast any outage.

panels.title: Janitor deadline hit
panels.description: Whether the janitor's last pass ran out of time. 1 means it hit its deadline and left work undone.

panels.title: Janitor pass errors
panels.description: Errors reported by the janitor's passes in its last run. Any value above 0 means a pass failed (see the error log).

panels.title: Oldest unexamined age
panels.description: Age of the oldest worktree the janitor has not examined yet, by pass. A value that keeps growing means the janitor cannot keep up.

panels.title: Orphan last event age
panels.description: Time since the orphan sweep last recorded an event. A very large value means the sweep is not running. window: fixed - the 7d lookback only has to outlast any outage.

panels.title: Worktree census duration
panels.description: How long the last worktree census took. A value near the scan budget means the census is about to be cut short.

panels.title: Sessions by state
panels.description: Sessions per state and liveness. Many live=false rows in working or needs_input mean sessions died without being closed.

targets.expr: sum by (state, live) (max by (state, live, pool, pgrouter_role) (last_over_time(ccpool_session_states{pool=~"$pool",pgrouter_role=~"$role"}[35m])))

panels.title: Sessions by role
panels.description: Sessions per role and pool (all states). A role that is missing or unlabelled when it should have sessions points at a launch problem.

targets.expr: sum by (pgrouter_role, pool) (max by (state, live, pool, pgrouter_role) (last_over_time(ccpool_session_states{pool=~"$pool",pgrouter_role=~"$role"}[35m])))

panels.title: Sessions over time by pool
panels.description: Live sessions over time, stacked by pool. A flat line at the pool maximum means the pool is saturated.

targets.expr: sum by (pool) (max by (state, live, pool, pgrouter_role) (last_over_time(ccpool_session_states{live="true",pool=~"$pool",pgrouter_role=~"$role"}[35m])))

panels.title: Reap closures by reason
panels.description: Sessions the reaper closed, by reason (idle_ttl, cap_eviction, dead_needs_input_ttl and others), per dashboard interval (counters are seeded with a zero sample per pool and reason, so a short window works). window: $__rate_interval; quiet reasons read 0. A burst of cap_eviction means the pool is oversubscribed; dead_needs_input_ttl means abandoned sessions waiting on a human.

panels.title: Phantoms pruned
panels.description: Phantom session records the reaper pruned, per dashboard interval (counter seeded at zero). window: $__rate_interval; reads 0 when quiet. A steady non-zero rate means sessions keep disappearing without a close.

panels.title: Cancels by outcome
panels.description: Session cancels, by outcome, per dashboard interval (counter seeded at zero). window: $__rate_interval; reads 0 when quiet. Outcomes other than success mean a cancel did not take effect.

panels.title: Janitor funnel
panels.description: The janitor's last pass: candidates, examined, cached, kept, unexamined and reclaimed worktrees. Many unexamined candidates, or nothing reclaimed while the worktree count climbs, means the janitor is not keeping up.

panels.title: Janitor phase seconds
panels.description: Wall time of each janitor phase in its last pass. A phase that grows toward the pass deadline will start hitting it.

panels.title: Run duration by pool
panels.description: p50 and p95 duration of a session run (launch or resume), by pool. A p95 that keeps rising means runs are getting slower or stuck. A run ended by the hook is counted at the reaper's next sweep (up to 300 s late). Counter panels require delta temporality end to end.

panels.title: Run duration by result
panels.description: p50 and p95 duration of a session run by how it ended. Long idle_ttl runs are normal; long runs that end in handler or exited errors are not.

panels.title: Sessions closed by pool and result
panels.description: Runs ended over the selected time range, by pool and result (idle_ttl, cap_eviction, operator, handler, exited, dead_needs_input_ttl). A large handler or exited share means runs are failing.

panels.title: Launch outcomes
panels.description: Session launch outcomes by pool, outcome and route, per dashboard interval (counter seeded at zero). window: $__rate_interval. Anything other than a success outcome means launches are failing.

panels.title: Capacity live vs max
panels.description: Live sessions against the pool maximum. Live pinned at max means the pool is full and launches will queue.

panels.title: Live session tokens
panels.description: Tokens in live sessions, by pool and role. A session that keeps growing without finishing is burning budget.

targets.expr:
label_replace(sum by (pool, pgrouter_role) (max by (session_id) (pa_monitor_session_tokens)
  * on (session_id) group_left (pool, pgrouter_role)
    label_replace(
      max by (claude_session_id, pool, pgrouter_role) (last_over_time(ccpool_session_info{pool=~"$pool", pgrouter_role=~"$role"}[35m])),
      "session_id", "$1", "claude_session_id", "(.*)"
    )), "pgrouter_role", "unlabelled", "pgrouter_role", "^$")

panels.title: Output tokens by pool and role
panels.description: Output tokens produced by finished sessions, by pool and role. A role whose output suddenly stops or spikes needs a look. A series with no role is shown as unlabelled.

panels.title: Worktrees over time
panels.description: Handler worktree count over time (the janitor census). A line that only climbs means worktrees are leaking.

panels.title: ccpool CPU
panels.description: CPU used by ccpool processes, in cores, by app. Sustained high CPU means a runaway ccpool process.

panels.title: ccpool memory
panels.description: Memory footprint of ccpool processes, by app. A footprint that keeps growing means a leak.

panels.title: ccpool disk write
panels.description: Disk write rate of ccpool processes, by app. Sustained heavy writes mean a process is churning the disk.

panels.title: Retries and exhausted
panels.description: Retries by class and genuinely exhausted retry policies, by pool, per dashboard interval (counters seeded at zero). window: $__rate_interval; reads 0 when quiet. Any exhausted retry means a launch gave up.

panels.title: Dead-but-working
panels.description: Sessions recorded as working whose process is gone and that nobody closed (rows closed by the pg-router handler or a reap are excluded). Any value above 0 means a session died without being closed. Zero is shown only while the exporter is reporting capacity; a dead exporter shows No data, not a green 0.

targets.expr: sum(max by (state, live, pool, pgrouter_role) (last_over_time(ccpool_session_states{state="working",live="false"}[35m]))) or (vector(0) and on() (max(last_over_time(ccpool_pool_capacity[35m])) >= 0))

panels.title: Error log (jsonl sources)
panels.description: WARN and ERROR lines from the ccpool and handler event logs. Any line is a fault to read.

panels.title: Session records by kind
panels.description: Registry records per kind, summed over the selected pools. live: tmux session present. dead_closed: not live and closed since its last activity (deleted after the closed-row retention). dead_unclosed: not live and nobody closed it, the fault signal. Any dead_unclosed above 0 for an hour is worth reading.

panels.title: Error log (raw sources)
panels.description: WARN and ERROR lines from the raw launchd logs of the janitor, daemon and pool-metrics handlers (matched on the level text, as these sources carry no reliable severity). Any line is a fault to read.

list.name: ccpool version
list.expr: max by (component, version) (last_over_time(ccpool_build_info[35m])) unless max by (component, version) (last_over_time(ccpool_build_info[35m] offset 35m))
